records.title: Consulate and export-company address for a wagon-sale instruction
records.header_literal: A) NKJ FUER RAT (6.50 a.m., November 16th); 0700 (16) 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-254
records.readable_german: Deutsches Generalkonsulat Odessa. Nr. ?? AUSSENUKRA. An DEUTSCHEEN Bevollmaechtigten Odessa. Fuer Ausfuhrgesellschaft. Abt. RM ? Ihr Telegramm
records.meaning: The first part gives the German consulate at Odessa, an unresolved numbered reference, the Odessa representative and an export company as address or routing information. It then begins a reference to a previous telegram. The spelling DEUTSCHEEN and AUSSENUKRA are retained without silently normalizing them.
notes: All 254 coordinates are present in the printed source and decode without repair. The earlier OCR split the first row from the rest; the complete native body is now used.
DEUTSCHEEN is retained with both E letters. AUSSENUKRA, ABT and RM remain unexpanded, and RM is not treated as a currency amount.

The three question marks are different unresolved square cells FD, GF and GD. They cannot be assigned independently or given the same label under an injective completion. No reference number is inferred.

records.title: Wagon Magdeburg sale request with opaque DAMM LADWIG phrase
records.header_literal: A) NKJ FUER RAT (6.50 a.m., November 16th); 0700 (16) 2 TLE; 2 TL RICHI-236
records.readable_german: Zweitausendundachtzig. Ersuchen Waggon Magdeburg neuntausendneunhundertzehn. DAMM LADWIG bestmoeglichst zu verkaufen. Auswaertig.
records.meaning: The continuation refers to the telegram with the spelled-out number zweitausendundachtzig and requests a sale on the best possible terms involving the wagon identified by Magdeburg and neuntausendneunhundertzehn. DAMM LADWIG remains opaque in the primary edition; it is not treated as a confirmed person, cargo description or instruction to sell the contents.
notes: The native 236-coordinate body is preserved. The initial unresolved square label is changed to Z in ZWEITAUSEND as one observed-coordinate substitution; this is not a free fill of an unknown square cell.
Both long numbers remain spelled out exactly as recovered. No wagon identity is independently established from those words.
The primary reading retains DAMM LADWIG. Conditional LADUNG, SAMT LADUNG and DANN LADUNG alternatives are separately priced, and none is silently substituted into the primary meaning.
SAMT LADUNG and DANN LADUNG each require nine observed changes from the source, including the initial Z proposal; coordinate cost alone does not choose between them.

limits: All native source slots remain in printed order; no insertion, deletion or reordering.
Unknown square cells remain globally coupled and injective. Roundtrip completion witnesses are explicitly nonhistorical.
Observed-coordinate substitutions and source-mask fills are priced separately. A source-compatible word proposal is not proof of unique historical wording.
